dataset.name: Photosynthetic and stomatal response, and leaf traits, of two pine species, Talladega National Forest, Alabama, 2023
description: Photosynthetic response to irradiance (AQ), CO2 (ACi) and stomatal response to irradiance measurements on two pine species common to the southeast United States, long leaf pine, Pinus palustris Mill., and loblolly pine, Pinus taeda L.. Data were collected in June 2023 within the Oakmulgee District of the Talladega National Forest in west-central Alabama at the NEON site (TALL). Measurements were made with four LI-COR LI-6800 and one LI-COR LI-6400XT gas exchange systems. ACi and AQ curves enable the estimation of photosynthetic parameters (e.g., Vcmax, Jmax, Rd, aQY), while stomatal response curves enable the estimation of stomatal slope and intercept parameters. Foliar trait data (needle dimensions, leaf mass per area, leaf nitrogen concentration) is provided for all gas exchange samples. The data package files include multiple raw and processed data files (csv), metadata files (csv), the complete instrument output for all measurements in .zip format, and a pdf describing the experimental protocol.

measurementTechnique:
Plant material:
This dataset was measured in the Oakmulgee District of the Talladega National Forest in west-central Alabama at the NEON flux tower site (NEON-TALL; https://www.neonscience.org/field-sites/tall). Two common species were sampled, long leaf pine, Pinus palustris Mill., and loblolly pine, Pinus taeda L. Sampling was conducted over a hillslope gradient from three elevations. Branches were collected via shotgun sampling, using a 12-gauge shotgun and steel bird shot. Once branches fell, they were immediately recut under water to prevent cavitation or embolism of the xylem, and placed into a shaded area where the gas exchange measurements were performed.

Leaf-level gas exchange:
Five portable photosynthesis systems were used, one LI-COR 6400XT and four LI-COR 6800s. Stomatal response curves were performed exclusively with the LI-6800s, and all instruments were used for ACi and AQ curves. Before beginning each curve, two fascicles (6 needles) was placed in the instrument cuvette under stable conditions (1800 μmol m-2s-1 PPFD, CO2 415 μmol mol−1 air, Tair 25-33 ºC, flow rate ≥ 450 µmol s-1) and allowed to acclimate to these conditions for a minimum of 45 minutes. Needles were spread apart to prevent self shading and each sample was checked for leaks.
ACi and AQ curves were generally measured sequentially on the same set of needles. In a few cases only ACi or only AQ were measured. For the ACi curves, the reference CO2 concentration of the gas injected into the leaf chamber was adjusted sequentially, as follows: 415, 300, 250, 175, 125, 70, 50, 415, 415, 415, 475, 575, 675, 800, 1000, 1400, 1800 μmol mol−1 air. After each CO2 level change, the reference and sample chambers were matched, then a log taken after stability was reached, measured as the standard deviation of CO2R < 0.75 and A < 0.2 over 20 seconds, with a wait time of 60 - 200 seconds. During these curves the irradiance level was maintained at 1800 μmol m-2s-1 PPFD.
After the CO2 response curve, the needles were again allowed to acclimate under stable conditions. For the AQ curves, the irradiance level inside the leaf chamber was adjusted sequentially as follows: 2000, 1800, 1500, 1250, 1000, 750, 600, 500, 375, 250, 180, 125, 100, 75, 60, 50, 30, 20, and 0 μmol m-2s-1 PPFD. Measurements were logged when stability of standard deviation of A < 0.2 and Qin < 1 over 20 seconds was reached, with a wait time of 60 - 200 seconds.
For stomatal response curves, rates of A and gsw were recorded at five irradiance levels (1800, 400, 90, 40, and 0 μmol m-2s-1 PPFD). Leaves were acclimated to each irradiance level for a minimum of 20 minutes, or until conductance was stable. At 0 µmol m⁻² the LI-COR head and surrounding needles were covered with a light proof cloth. An automatic logging program was used to record rates every 10 seconds for the duration of the curve. Five of these points (50 s average) were taken to constitute the stabilized rates of A and gsw at each irradiance level.
Following completion of each curve, the fascicles were removed from the chamber and the needle length and fascicle diameter were measured using digital calipers. Then, using the equations presented in Johnson (1984) we calculated the leaf area of the needles. This needle area value was used for all subsequent gas exchange calculations.
The files included in this data package follow the ESS-DIVE Leaf-level gas exchange data and metadata reporting format (Ely et al, 2021).
